task.description:
Combined Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for `docs/issues/ISS-0114.yaml` (queue task 182, GH#368). Read it in full -- it is detailed and this dispatch does not restate it. The failure: `Letflow.EngineConcurrencyTest` at `test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs:365` raised Postgrex `42P01 undefined_table` on `tenant_<id>.instance_projections` from `Letflow.Engine.insert_instance_projection/8`, observed once in a full-suite run and correctly filed as UNATTRIBUTED rather than folded into a known family.

STEP 0.5 -- REGISTRY LOOKUP. Search `docs/issues/*.yaml` for `status: resolved` entries whose description mentions similar symptoms (a tenant-schema table missing during a live test that provisioned it). ISS-0109 is already named as the same symptom FAMILY but explicitly NOT the same issue (different module, frame, missing relation) -- confirm that reasoning yourself rather than accepting it, and check whether the identical root cause has recurred since ISS-0114 was filed (a fix that didn't actually fix the underlying issue). If recurring, severity is at least MAJOR regardless of the original MINOR.

STEP 1 -- DIAGNOSE, DO NOT FIX. Reproduce if you can (this is a concurrency-timing-sensitive failure against a live Postgres, so a single run may not reproduce it -- if it doesn't reproduce in N attempts, say so and explain what that does and does not tell you, rather than treating non-reproduction as exoneration). Read `test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs:365` and its surrounding test, and `Letflow.Engine.insert_instance_projection/8` in `lib/letflow/engine.ex`, to understand the actual code path: what provisions the tenant schema, what creates `instance_projections`, and what race window could let a concurrent test observe the schema present but the table not yet created (or already dropped).

THE ISSUE'S OWN SUGGESTED FIRST STEP: adopt `Letflow.TenantFixture` (`test/support/tenant_fixture.ex`) in this test module -- it is not adopted yet (confirm this yourself; ISS-0112, still open, tracks the general adoption gap). Its `capture_schema_state/1` (read its actual implementation, don't assume the shape from the name) answers exactly the open questions here: was the registry row present, was the schema present, which tables were present/missing, which migrations were applied. If you can get this test to fail again (or construct a targeted reproduction of the race under load/concurrency), capture the schema state at the moment of failure using this helper and report EXACTLY what it shows -- that is the diagnosis this issue is asking for, not a guess from reading the code alone.

Write the root cause (not just the symptom) into your handoff's `result.summary`: which function creates `instance_projections`, whether it is synchronous with schema provisioning or eventually-consistent, what the race window actually is, and what a fix needs to change (a missing await/synchronization point, a wrong assumption about migration completion, or something else). Do NOT implement the fix. If you conclude this needs `Letflow.TenantFixture` adopted first (to make future occurrences attributable) as a prerequisite, distinguish that from the actual root-cause fix -- they may be two different pieces of work, and CODE-DESIGNER needs to know which is which.
acceptance_criteria: The registry lookup was actually performed -- named which resolved issues were checked and why ISS-0109 is confirmed (not merely accepted) to be a different mechanism

At least one real reproduction attempt was made (either reproducing the original failure or constructing a targeted concurrency scenario), and if it did not reproduce, what that does and does not establish is stated explicitly rather than treated as exoneration
The actual code path (schema/table provisioning timing vs. insert_instance_projection/8's own assumptions) is read and traced, not inferred from the error message alone
If a reproduction succeeded, Letflow.TenantFixture.capture_schema_state/1 (or equivalent) was used to capture real state at failure time, with the actual captured values reported
The root cause (not just symptom) is stated: what creates instance_projections, what race window exists, and what a fix needs to change
No fix is implemented -- this step produces a diagnosis only, routed to CODE-DESIGNER next
The relationship between a TenantFixture-adoption prerequisite (if concluded necessary) and the actual root-cause fix is stated as two distinguishable pieces of work, not conflated

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 -- REGISTRY LOOKUP (performed, not skipped). Checked every docs/issues/*.yaml entry whose description mentions a tenant-schema/table absence during a live test that provisioned it: the resolved lineage ISS-0048 -> ISS-0050 -> ISS-0060 -> ISS-0062 -> ISS-0064 (all status: resolved) documents orphaned tenant_schemas rows accumulating across mix test invocations with no reaper, fixed by ISS-0064 shipping Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2 (test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex). None of these five is a match for ISS-0114's own symptom (they are pre-test guard failures against pre-existing orphaned rows, not a live INSERT failing mid-test) but ISS-0064's fix is exactly the mechanism this diagnosis lands on below -- see 'why this is not a fresh root cause' below. Also checked: ISS-0109 (status: instrumented, not resolved) and its successor ISS-0116 (status: instrumented) -- both explicitly named in ISS-0114's own text as 'same family, not same issue'. CONFIRMED, not merely accepted: ISS-0109's refuted mechanism was 'a teardown path drops the schema out from under the SAME test that just provisioned it, ~1 second later' -- established false for its own failure-3 case by three independent grounds (schema_name_for_tenant/1 is a pure closure only the failing test's own on_exit could have named; ExUnit runs on_exit synchronously and the module is async:false; the DROP used IF EXISTS and merely succeeded against an already-absent schema). ISS-0109's text ALSO says 'TenantSchemaReaper is EXCLUDED for the 1-second-old-row case' -- note precisely: that exclusion is scoped to the ~1s-old row in failure 3, NOT a blanket exclusion of the reaper as a mechanism in general. ISS-0114's own row is not 1-second-old: AC1's 100-sequential-instance-creation loop plus AC4's own 100-instance provision-and-complete-all run inside a 612.1s full-suite invocation, so a tenant provisioned early in that run and still in active use minutes later is squarely the case ISS-0109 did NOT rule the reaper out for. CRITICAL FIND: ISS-0110 (status: open, severity MAJOR, filed same run as ISS-0109) already names this exact mechanism verbatim: 'TenantSchemaReaper's 300s min_age can no longer outlive the suite (564-609s), so a nested/concurrent mix test's pre-suite sweep can DROP a live run's tenant schema.' ISS-0110 is still OPEN/unfixed. RECURRENCE CALL: this is not a resolved issue recurring in the strict sense (ISS-0064 was never marked resolved-then-regressed; its fix, the reaper, is what introduced this new, DIFFERENT failure mode -- too-eager cross-invocation cleanup instead of ISS-0064's original no-cleanup-at-all problem) -- but ISS-0114 is best read as a live occurrence of ISS-0110's already-diagnosed, still-unfixed MAJOR hazard, not a new root cause. Per WF-03 Step 0.5's rule ('if recurring, flag severity as at least MAJOR regardless of original severity'), recommend ISS-0114's severity be raised from MINOR to at least MAJOR to match ISS-0110, since it is evidence of that same live, unpatched channel rather than a one-off. 

STEP 1 -- DIAGNOSE (reproduced via constructed targeted scenario, not from prose). First attempted the plain approach: ran test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs alone (3 runs) and alongside 12 other tenant-provisioning-heavy modules (engine_cancel_instance_test.exs, engine_complete_task_test.exs, engine_execution_error_test.exs, engine_plugin_error_routing_test.exs, engine_sub_process_test.exs, engine_test.exs, engine_variable_schema_merge_test.exs, definitions/promotion_test.exs, definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs, definitions/rollback_test.exs, engine/reconstruction_test.exs, role_registry_test.exs) in one mix test invocation, seed 42: 156/156 passed in 94.3s, confirmed via the run's own 'Finished in 94.3 seconds (0.00s async, 94.3s sync)' line that every DataCase-based module in this repo runs SYNCHRONOUSLY (async: false), so no amount of within-process test concurrency can itself race two tenants' migrations against each other -- the race, if real, has to be cross-invocation (two separate mix test/BEAM processes sharing one Postgres database), matching ISS-0110's own framing exactly. NON-REPRODUCTION IN THIS FORM ESTABLISHES: that a single mix test invocation, run in isolation or as a modest multi-file batch, cannot trigger this failure by itself in the ~600s-plus-only window this family needs -- it does NOT establish the code path is safe, because the failure's own precondition (a second, concurrently-running mix test invocation against the SAME database, with a tenant provisioned by the first run being both >300s old and still in active use) was not present in that run. CONSTRUCTED REPRODUCTION (succeeded): wrote a throwaway probe test (test/letflow/tmp_iss0114_repro_test.exs, deleted before this handoff -- never committed) that (1) provisioned a real tenant via Tenant.create_changeset/3 + TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 + TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1, exactly matching engine_concurrency_test.exs's own hand-rolled provisioned_tenant/0; (2) confirmed instance_projections genuinely exists right after provisioning+replay (BEFORE SWEEP: instance_projections present? true); (3) called Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans(Letflow.Repo, 0) -- min_age_seconds: 0 standing in for 'this row is now older than a SECOND, concurrently-running invocation's 300s default cutoff', the real-world condition satisfied by any tenant provisioned in the first ~5 minutes of this repo's own 564-612s full-suite runs -- which reclaimed the row (SWEEP RESULT: {:ok, %{reclaimed: 1, skipped_invalid_format: 0}}), i.e. DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE plus DELETE FROM tenant_schemas plus DELETE FROM tenants, exactly reclaim_row/2's three statements; then (4) attempted the SAME operation ISS-0114 observed -- an insert into <schema>.instance_projections via Letflow.EventStore.InstanceProjection.insert_changeset/1 |> Repo.insert(prefix: schema_name), the identical call insert_instance_projection/8 makes. RESULT: raised ** (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 42P01 (undefined_table) relation "tenant_8ea6fa0feed1484f9b2997d4ccc20b8b.instance_projections" does not exist -- byte-for-byte the same error class, same relation-name shape, same raising call site shape (a bare Repo.insert(prefix:) against a schema whose catalog entry is gone) as ISS-0114's own report. Letflow.TenantFixture.capture_schema_state/1 called immediately after, on the same tenant_id, per this issue's own suggested first step: returned {:ok, %{schema_name: "tenant_8ea6fa0feed1484f9b2997d4ccc20b8b", tenant_id: "8ea6fa0f-eed1-484f-9b29-97d4ccc20b8b", registration_present?: false, provisioned_at: nil, migrations_applied_at: nil, schema_present?: false, tables_present: [], tables_missing: [all 19 expected tables], applied_versions: [], manifest_versions: [the full 31-entry manifest], versions_missing: [], observed_at_utc: ~N[2026-08-21 13:43:00.572000], db_now: ~N[2026-08-21 13:43:01.429896], pg_backend_pid: 508053}. registration_present? false AND schema_present? false together are the signature of a FULL reclaim_row/2 sweep (schema dropped, tenant_schemas row deleted, tenants row deleted) -- NOT a bare mid-schema table drop, and NOT the on_exit-teardown-ordering mechanism ISS-0109 refuted for its own failure 3 (that teardown's DROP target was the SAME test's own tenant, leaving no way for THIS test's later insert to still name it; here the reclaim is a genuinely separate code path, callable from any process holding a Postgres connection to the same database, with zero coupling to which test/process provisioned the row). NOTE ON ISS-0214: a separate live capture (registration_present?: true, schema_present?: false) exists in that record from the same session -- structurally DIFFERENT from this reproduction's signature (registration_present? false here) and therefore NOT the same mechanism as this diagnosis; ISS-0214 remains a distinct, still-unexplained case and is out of scope for this diagnosis. 

CODE PATH TRACED (read directly, not inferred from the error message): Letflow.Engine.persist/11 (lib/letflow/engine.ex:829-926) runs an Ecto.Multi whose first step, Multi.run(:instance_projection, ...), calls insert_instance_projection/8 (line 1003), which does `%InstanceProjection{} |> InstanceProjection.insert_changeset(attrs) |> repo.insert(prefix: prefix)` (lines 1022-1024) -- this is the exact call this diagnosis reproduced directly. Table creation is synchronous with schema provisioning in the normal case: TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:164-202) runs CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS inside a transaction with an advisory lock, and TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1 (lines 238-264) runs Ecto.Migrator.run(Repo, migrations, :up, prefix: schema_name) synchronously -- by the time replay_migrations/1 returns {:ok, _}, instance_projections is genuinely committed and visible to any new Postgres session (confirmed directly: BEFORE SWEEP check above). There is NO race in provisioning/replay itself, matching ISS-0109/ISS-0116's own prior finding that this half of the pipeline has no production defect. THE RACE WINDOW is entirely in test/test_helper.exs's suite-boundary contract: `Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans()` runs once before ExUnit.start() and once via ExUnit.after_suite/1 (test/test_helper.exs:1-5) -- correct ONLY if 'currently active' really is the empty set at both of THIS invocation's own boundaries, which test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's own moduledoc argues but ALSO admits ('in this or any concurrently-running mix test invocation') is not guaranteed once a second mix test process shares the same Postgres database (same host/port, same MIX_TEST_PARTITION -- ISS-0110 names Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.Test's own Port.open({:spawn_executable,...}) inheriting the parent's env as one concrete way this happens, and this diagnosis run independently observed, live, a second/sibling session exhausting this same database's max_connections=100 with 80+ idle connections moments before this run started -- direct confirmation concurrent invocations against this exact database are not hypothetical here). sweep_orphans/2's ONLY safety margin is @default_min_age_seconds = 300 (test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex:43) with NO liveness tracking of any kind (unlike Letflow.SandboxPool's owner-monitor, per ISS-0110's own comparison). Once a full-suite run's own wall-clock (measured 564-612s across four recorded runs, including this issue's own originating 612.1s run) exceeds 300s, a tenant provisioned in that run's first ~5 minutes and STILL in active use is a valid sweep_orphans/2 target for any OTHER invocation's boundary sweep -- exactly engine_concurrency_test.exs's own shape: AC1 provisions a tenant then sequentially creates 100 instances before its first assertion, and AC4 does the same via provision_and_complete_all!/2, so a tenant that sits provisioned-but-still-being-populated for several minutes inside a long full suite is architecturally exactly what this hazard needs. ROOT CAUSE STATEMENT: instance_projections is created synchronously and correctly by TenantProvisioning; the table is not actually missing due to any provisioning/replay defect. What actually removes it in ISS-0114's case is Letflow.TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2 -- test-only, but with unscoped, unbounded blast radius across ANY mix test invocation sharing the same Postgres database -- reclaiming (DROP SCHEMA CASCADE + delete tenant_schemas + delete tenants) a tenant row that is still actively in use by a DIFFERENT, concurrently-running invocation, once that row is older than the reaper's fixed 300s min_age -- a threshold shorter than this repo's own measured full-suite runtime (564-612s). This is precisely ISS-0110's own already-filed, still-open diagnosis; this run's contribution is a live, capture_schema_state-instrumented reproduction directly on ISS-0114's own exact error shape and call site, not a new independent root cause. WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE: NOT a fix to Letflow.Engine.insert_instance_projection/8 or to any provisioning/replay code (none of it is defective) -- the fix belongs entirely in test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's own liveness model, exactly as ISS-0110 already states: either real liveness tracking (a session/PID marker per row so a sweep can tell 'this row belongs to a currently-running invocation' rather than guessing from age alone) or scoping a sweep to rows this invocation could not possibly own (e.g. its own PID's lineage) -- ISS-0110 explicitly warns against just raising min_age, since that trades this hazard for reintroducing ISS-0064's original orphan-accumulation problem. CODE-DESIGNER should design against ISS-0110's own affected_files (test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex, lib/letflow/design/iss064-orphaned-tenant-schemas-fix.md, test/test_helper.exs), not against engine.ex or engine_concurrency_test.exs, which are only where ISS-0114's own symptom happened to surface. TENANTFIXTURE ADOPTION -- DISTINCT, SEPARATE PIECE OF WORK: ISS-0114's own suggested first step (adopt Letflow.TenantFixture in engine_concurrency_test.exs, per ISS-0112's still-open general adoption gap) is a DIAGNOSTIC-INSTRUMENTATION improvement, not a root-cause fix -- it would make a FUTURE occurrence in this module self-report via capture_schema_state/1 and a LETFLOW_TENANT_FIXTURE marker instead of a bare Postgrex error, exactly as ISS-0116/ISS-0115 already did for their own modules, but it does not stop the reaper from reclaiming a live tenant. These are two separable pieces of work: (a) adopt TenantFixture in engine_concurrency_test.exs (small, mechanical, ISS-0112-shaped, safe to do independently and first if desired for better future attributability) vs. (b) fix TenantSchemaReaper's liveness model (ISS-0110's own scope, the actual root-cause removal ISS-0114 needs to be genuinely resolved rather than merely instrumented). Recommend routing (b) to CODE-DESIGNER against ISS-0110's own filing (this run's diagnosis is strong corroborating evidence ISS-0110 should be picked up and fixed, not merely left open), and noting (a) as an optional, separate, lower-priority companion task equivalent to ISS-0112's remaining scope. STATUS CALL: result.status is PARTIAL rather than PASS/BLOCKED because the diagnosis is complete and strongly evidenced but points at an ALREADY-FILED, MAJOR, still-open issue (ISS-0110) rather than a wholly new one -- ORCH should decide whether this issue closes as a duplicate/instance pointing at ISS-0110 (with severity raised to MAJOR) rather than proceeding through its own separate Step 2 fix-design cycle, to avoid two parallel fix-design efforts converging on the same file.
issues: ISS-0110 (status: open, severity MAJOR) already describes the exact root-cause mechanism this diagnosis reproduces and confirms live: TenantSchemaReaper's 300s min_age no longer outlives a 564-612s full suite. Recommend ORCH route ISS-0114's actual fix through ISS-0110 rather than opening a second, parallel fix-design track against the same files.
Recommend raising ISS-0114's own severity field from MINOR to MAJOR to reflect that it is a live occurrence of ISS-0110's already-known hazard, not a one-off unattributed flake.

ISS-0214 (status: open) carries a structurally different capture (registration_present?: true, schema_present?: false) from the same session -- explicitly NOT the same mechanism as this diagnosis (which shows registration_present?: false) and left untouched/out of scope here.
result.next_action: ORCH decision needed before Step 2: this diagnosis attributes ISS-0114 to ISS-0110's already-filed, still-open MAJOR hazard (TenantSchemaReaper cross-invocation reclaim of a live, >300s-old tenant), not a new root cause in lib/letflow/engine.ex or engine_concurrency_test.exs. Recommend ORCH route the actual fix through ISS-0110's own queue task rather than dispatching a separate CODE-DESIGNER cycle against ISS-0114, to avoid two parallel designs converging on test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex. If ORCH still wants a fix designed under ISS-0114's own task id, route to CODE-DESIGNER against test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex (liveness tracking or invocation-scoped sweep, per ISS-0110's own 'what a fix needs to decide' note -- not raising min_age) plus optionally, as a separate lower-priority companion, TenantFixture adoption in test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs (ISS-0112-shaped, diagnostic only, does not remove the root cause).
